behavioral_cases.review_note: PDF pp.93–95: Karuizawa forcefully rejects a phone photo without her permission; Machida, not Karuizawa, convinces the hostile girls to stop. Consent and rescue are distinct acts.
PDF pp.159–161: Karuizawa refuses Manabe's pressured apology after disputing the café accusation; social defiance does not independently prove the accusation false.
PDF pp.199–200: Karuizawa verbally resists Kiyotaka's sexual threats while physically trapped; freezing and later compliance are not consent or a stable capability.
PDF pp.231,234: Karuizawa is privately identified as Rabbit VIP in Kiyotaka's later account and checks his plan anxiously; others cannot retrospectively know this secret.
PDF pp.26–27: Sakura approaches Kiyotaka over difficult cabin relations, admitting simultaneous desire for company and solitude; only her self-reported anxiety is supported.
PDF pp.21–22: Kōenji dismisses a worker's warnings and gives an autograph with predicted future value; no financial realization of that boast is observed.
PDF pp.14–16: Hirata cancels a previously planned Karuizawa lunch to speak to Kiyotaka; observed concern is not a permanent partner priority.
PDF pp.17–19: Hirata requests private indirect outreach to Horikita and accepts Kiyotaka's doubts; Horikita's endorsement is not achieved by this case.
PDF pp.173–176: Hirata seeks a nonviolent remedy for Karuizawa but will not renounce help for other peers; his choice alienates her rather than ensuring safety.
PDF pp.180–182: Hirata describes guilt over Sugimura's bullying; the motivation is his testimony and must not be treated as an externally audited childhood record.
PDF pp.64–65: Suzune compares group membership to academic excellence and adjusts a tentative theory when it fails examples; no normative allocation method is discovered.
PDF pp.148–149: Suzune counters Ryūen's strategic threats and rejects the proposed coalition; Ichinose's refusal is her own separate decision.
PDF p.144: Kushida invites visitors into Dragon discussion without disclosing her own VIP status; inviting is not proving leader or information dominance.
PDF pp.50–51: Yukimura recommends keeping VIP information private but cannot force compliance from Karuizawa, who soon calls Hirata.
PDF pp.224–225: Yukimura unlocks and shows a switched phone, acting on a false incomplete account from Kiyotaka; successful deception ownership remains Kiyotaka's.
PDF pp.85–91: Machida's silence strategy carries Class A incentives and provokes Ichinose's objection; it is not a proven optimal strategy for all classes.
PDF p.95: Machida tells Manabe to stop unwanted photos and she backs down; this does not establish he knew which claimant told the truth.
PDF pp.190–193: Manabe participates in abusive group intimidation and assault against Karuizawa; it demonstrates wrongdoing, not justified punishment or a desirable tactic.
PDF pp.218–219: Hamaguchi originates the voluntary authentic-message inspection and shows his own device; he does not independently solve Rabbit's VIP identity.
PDF p.222: Ibuki displays her device and challenges hesitant peers; the visible email is not proof she is invariably honest or a school's allocation authority.
PDF pp.69–73: Ryūen probes Suzune about the substituted island leader; the audience withholds the identity, so he has not solved it at this moment.
PDF pp.145–149: Ryūen pitches a cooperative B/C–D scheme and asserts he knows Class C VIPs; Ichinose expressly refuses, so no alliance is consummated.
PDF pp.239–240: Ryūen correctly says Kushida was Dragon VIP, claiming early deduction from Suzune's reactions; discovery timing and sole mechanism are unverified.
PDF pp.81–82: Ichinose initiates Rabbit introductions and volunteers to facilitate when nobody else does; rivals remain free to oppose her agenda.
PDF pp.29–30: Kiyotaka compares three school summons with unequal times and forms a preliminary scheduling hypothesis; not a solved Zodiac grouping rule.
PDF p.23: Kiyotaka reactivates the bellhop's complaint about Kōenji to escape socially; no sustained manipulation or universal response is established.
PDF pp.17–18: Kiyotaka cautions Hirata that indirect mediation could estrange Suzune; only Hirata's reconsideration, not Suzune's conversion, is observed.
PDF p.83: Kiyotaka cooperatively addresses Rabbit and asks Sotomura to react, gaining responses without identifying any VIP.
PDF p.148: Kiyotaka verbally introduces a conditional Class A/D counteralliance to deter Ryūen; it is a strategic claim, not an actual pact.
PDF pp.166–169: Kiyotaka consults Chabashira about using points for bounded school alterations; teacher's hypothetical answer is not an authorized transaction.
PDF pp.185–188: Kiyotaka actively lures peers to an isolated setting knowing their hostility; this is harmful staging of an assault, not safe tactical guidance.
PDF pp.194–201: Kiyotaka threatens, sexually harasses and exploits Karuizawa's trauma while she is fearful; any apparent compliance cannot be interpreted as consent.
PDF pp.202–203: Kiyotaka promises protection using an earlier stairwell photo and demands compliance; the resulting agreement follows serious coercion.
PDF pp.220,230–231: Kiyotaka creates a multi-stage phone/SIM deception; the accurate identity of the real VIP is late private knowledge, not public Rabbit knowledge.
PDF pp.227–232: Kiyotaka allows Ichinose to challenge his false appearance of VIP status and responds; Ichinose's independent SIM-lock deduction is not his feat.
PDF pp.146–149: Ichinose rejects Ryūen's proposed class alliance under trust and reputational concerns; neither Horikita nor Kiyotaka owns that refusal.
PDF pp.86–90: Ichinose counters Machida's no-search policy with long-term class-rank incentives; does not independently reveal the school VIP allocation.
PDF pp.218–220: Ichinose endorses Hamaguchi's display experiment and readies her phone, but Kiyotaka interrupts BEFORE her email is shown.
PDF pp.227–232: Ichinose calls Kiyotaka's number, verifies device-lock loopholes and names Karuizawa as a prediction; an early termination preempts her answer.
PDF pp.232–233: Ichinose opts not to submit against Rabbit and hopes a rival will make a mistaken early guess; Morishige is an uncorroborated suspect.
PDF pp.166–169: Chabashira describes limited school purchases with private points but never commits to selling unlimited exceptions.
PDF pp.141–142: Katsuragi explicitly refuses Ichinose's request to have Class A members discuss VIP identities; the claim extends no farther than this examination.
PDF pp.202–203: Karuizawa accepts Kiyotaka's proposed protection and cooperation under credible pressure, without freely bargained trust or consent.
